back2basics.concept: Space Economy and Indigenous Technology Development
back2basics.text: The space economy includes all activities related to manufacturing, launching, and using space technologies and services. Indigenous technology development means creating and innovating technologies within the country to reduce dependence on foreign sources. Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) is a method to inspect materials and components without causing damage, ensuring quality and safety in critical sectors like defence and aerospace.

2026-11-16-am-3bf26b786c.deck: India has transformed its space sector from a government-led model to a collaborative, industry-driven ecosystem with significant private participation and policy reforms. Concurrently, the Defence Ministry emphasizes indigenous innovation in advanced technologies like Non-Destructive Testing to enhance strategic self-reliance and operational reliability.

body.label: Government-led to collaborative model
body.text: India's space journey began with ISRO and the Department of Space leading government efforts, but reforms since 2020 have opened the entire space value chain to private players through institutions like IN-SPACe and NSIL.

body.label: Institutional framework and policy
body.text: The Indian Space Policy 2023 clearly defines roles: ISRO focuses on advanced research and national missions, while private enterprises undertake manufacturing, launch vehicle development, and space services.

body.label: Private sector growth and support
body.text: Space start-ups grew from one in 2014 to about 440 in 2026, with cumulative investments rising from US$100.5 million in 2021–22 to US$618.5 million by March 2026, supported by funding schemes like seed funds, Technology Adoption Fund, and a ₹1000 crore Venture Capital Fund.

body.label: Commercial and industrial outcomes
body.text: Private companies like Skyroot Aerospace and Agnikul Cosmos have launched rockets and satellites, while ISRO's launch vehicle technologies have been transferred to industry for production, strengthening domestic manufacturing.

body.label: Projected growth
body.text: India's space economy is projected to grow to about US$44 billion by 2033 and US$100 billion by 2040, aiming for around 8% of the global space economy.

sections.heading: How has India transformed its space economy?

body.label: Need for indigenous development
body.text: Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh emphasized that India must become a developer and innovator in advanced technologies, not just a user, to reduce dependencies and strengthen defence preparedness.

body.label: Focus on Non-Destructive Testing (NDT)
body.text: NDT technologies allow inspection of materials and components without damage, crucial for ensuring the quality, reliability, and safety of defence systems like missiles, aircraft, and spacecraft.

body.label: Quality assurance and strategic necessity
body.text: Embedding quality at every manufacturing stage prevents hidden defects that can jeopardize mission success; quality is essential for operational reliability and national security.

body.label: Technological advancements in inspection
body.text: Integration of AI, Machine Learning, Robotics, Advanced Sensors, Digital Twins, and Predictive Analytics is enhancing inspection speed, consistency, and accuracy in defence applications.

body.label: Collaborative innovation ecosystem
body.text: Innovation thrives when government, industry, academia, and research labs collaborate, supported by initiatives like iDEX and the Technology Development Fund.

back2basics.text: A transboundary water treaty is an agreement between two or more countries sharing a river or water resource to regulate its use and management. Such treaties ensure predictable water sharing, prevent conflicts, and promote cooperation on ecological and economic issues related to the river basin.

2026-11-16-am-aa30a32e3d.deck: The 30-year-old Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh is set to expire soon, and an expert has urged political leaders of both countries to support its temporary renewal for three to five years. This is important for UPSC aspirants to understand the challenges in transboundary water treaties and their impact on bilateral relations and resource management.

sections.heading: What is the current status of the Ganga Water Treaty?

body.label: Ensures predictable water supply
body.text: The treaty provides a legally binding framework for sharing Ganga waters, ensuring predictability in water flow, which Bangladesh depended on after suffering unpredictability between 1988 and 1996.

body.label: Agricultural and ecological impact
body.text: Without the treaty, India has no obligation to release water regularly, which could severely affect Bangladesh's agriculture sector, economy, and ecology, especially during the February agricultural season.

body.label: Water sharing formula
body.text: The treaty specifies water sharing at Farakka based on ten-day periods from January 1 to May 31, with detailed division formulas depending on water availability.

body.label: Urgent political agreement required
body.text: An immediate agreement between the political leaderships of both countries is necessary to keep the treaty operational and avoid reverting to past unpredictability.

back2basics.text: Counter-terrorism involves coordinated efforts by countries to prevent and respond to terrorist activities.
